1.why: verify-token only compares the submitted token's SHA-256 against the recovery record owned by the current session (ownedRecovery checks recovery.sessionId === session.id), so the code is bound to its requester.

2.why: A token is stored only in the session-bound recovery record and is validated exclusively against that record, so another session's token cannot be used elsewhere.

3.why: There is no session invalidation or rotation after the password is set — the same 'sid' session remains valid (and continues to the privacy/confirmation stages), so prior sessions persist.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and refuses to start without them, and HSTS is sent, though no explicit minimum TLS version is pinned (relies on Bun defaults).

5.why: Reset tokens are 32-byte CSPRNG values stored only as SHA-256 hashes and cleared after use, and passwords are hashed with bcrypt cost 12; no other user data is stored.

6.why: No email is actually generated or protected — the reset token is returned in the JSON response as 'mockToken' and displayed openly in the page and console, so there is no guarded email message.

7.why: Input is length-capped, email is regex-validated, token is validated against /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/, password policy is enforced server-side, and all output uses textContent (though validEmail's result is discarded via void).

8.why: Navigation is purely same-origin hash routing restricted to a whitelist of view names, with no user-controlled redirect targets and CSP form-action 'self'/base-uri 'none'.

9.why: There are no email templates at all; the simulated delivery notice is built with createElement/textContent so no user-supplied HTML or script can be embedded.

10.why: Error responses are generic with no stack traces, but the live reset token is deliberately printed to the on-page log panel and browser console ('Test reset token: ' + state.mockToken), exposing the secret.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and never persisted in plaintext, but the MFA secret is hardcoded in the source as const MFA_CODE = "246810" and echoed to the UI.

12.why: The static, hardcoded MFA code "246810" functions as a default credential that every recovery flow accepts.

13.why: Per-recovery attempt counters (ATTEMPT_LIMIT 5) with 60-second blocks for token/MFA/password plus per-IP sliding-window rate limits are enforced on every sensitive endpoint.

14.why: /api/recovery always returns the same generic 'If an eligible account is available…' message regardless of email validity or existence, and the UI states this explicitly.

15.why: Tokens come from crypto.getRandomValues (32 bytes / 64 hex chars), are single-use, expire in 15 minutes, and are tied to the specific session's recovery record.
